ACCESS_DENIED.title: Forbidden
ACCESS_DENIED.description: The caller is authenticated but not permitted to do what the request asks. Retrying with the same credentials will fail the same way; act as a user who holds the permission, or don't make the request.

ADDITION_PROHIBITED.title: Addition is prohibited
ADDITION_PROHIBITED.description: This relationship does not let a client add members to it. Don't retry the request; the relationship changes only in the ways the API documents for it.

APPLICATION_ERROR.title: Application error
APPLICATION_ERROR.description: The server failed to handle the request because of a fault on its side, not because of anything in the request. Retrying won't help; report it to the API's maintainers.

ATOMIC_OPERATIONS_INVALID.title: Atomic operations request is invalid
ATOMIC_OPERATIONS_INVALID.description: An operation in the Atomic Operations request is malformed: a missing or unknown `op`, or a broken `ref`, `href` or `data`. The server applied none of the batch; fix the operation at `source.pointer` and send the whole batch again.

ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_INVALID.title: Attribute value is invalid
ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_INVALID.description: The server could not accept the value of the attribute at `source.pointer`, for example a date-time it cannot parse. Correct the value and send the request again.
ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_INVALID.exampleDetail: The value for attribute "publishedAt" is invalid: Failed to parse time string (next blursday) at position 0 (n): The timezone could not be found in the database

AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED.title: Unauthorized
AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED.description: The request carried no credentials, or credentials the server rejected, such as an expired token. Authenticate, then send the request again with valid credentials.

CLIENT_GENERATED_ID_ALREADY_EXISTS.title: Client generated ID already exists
CLIENT_GENERATED_ID_ALREADY_EXISTS.description: A resource of this type already has the `id` the create request supplied. Generate a new id and send the request again, or update the existing resource instead.

CLIENT_GENERATED_ID_NOT_SUPPORTED.title: Client generated ID is not supported
CLIENT_GENERATED_ID_NOT_SUPPORTED.description: The create request supplied an `id`, but this resource type assigns its own ids. Leave `data.id` out and the server generates one.
CLIENT_GENERATED_ID_NOT_SUPPORTED.exampleDetail: Client generated ID '1' is not supported!

CLIENT_GENERATED_ID_REQUIRED.title: Required client generated ID
CLIENT_GENERATED_ID_REQUIRED.description: This resource type expects the client to choose the id, and the create request supplied none. Add `data.id` in the format the API documents and send the request again.
CLIENT_GENERATED_ID_REQUIRED.exampleDetail: A client generated ID must be used!

CURSOR_MALFORMED.title: Cursor is malformed
CURSOR_MALFORMED.description: The cursor in the named `page` parameter could not be decoded. Use cursors exactly as the server returned them in a previous page's `links`; never build or edit one.
CURSOR_MALFORMED.exampleDetail: The cursor supplied in 'page[after]' could not be decoded.

CURSOR_STALE.title: Cursor is stale
CURSOR_STALE.description: The cursor was issued for a different sort order than this request asks for, so it no longer marks a position in these results. Keep `sort` unchanged while paging, or start again from the first page.
CURSOR_STALE.exampleDetail: The cursor supplied in 'page[after]' was built for a different sort order and can no longer be used.

DATA_MEMBER_MISSING.title: Missing `data` member at the document's top level
DATA_MEMBER_MISSING.description: The request document has no top-level `data` member, which this request needs. Send the resource object or relationship linkage under `data`.
DATA_MEMBER_MISSING.exampleDetail: Missing `data` member at the document's top level!

FIELDSET_MEMBER_UNRECOGNIZED.title: Fieldset member is unrecognized
FIELDSET_MEMBER_UNRECOGNIZED.description: A `fields[TYPE]` parameter names a member that type does not have. Request only the attributes and relationships the type declares.
FIELDSET_MEMBER_UNRECOGNIZED.exampleDetail: Fields 'colour' requested for type 'articles' can't be recognized by the endpoint!

FILTERING_UNRECOGNIZED.title: Filtering parameter is unrecognized
FILTERING_UNRECOGNIZED.description: The request filtered on a key this endpoint does not declare. Filter only on the keys the API documents for this resource type.
FILTERING_UNRECOGNIZED.exampleDetail: Filtering parameter 'colour' can't be recognized by the endpoint!

FILTER_VALUE_INVALID.title: Filter value is invalid
FILTER_VALUE_INVALID.description: A `filter[...]` value fails the constraints that filter declares, for example text where a number is expected. Correct the value of the parameter named in `source.parameter`; each failed constraint is its own error.
FILTER_VALUE_INVALID.exampleDetail: The value supplied for 'filter[rating]' is invalid.

FULL_REPLACEMENT_PROHIBITED.title: Full replacement is prohibited
FULL_REPLACEMENT_PROHIBITED.description: This relationship cannot be replaced as a whole, for example by a `PATCH` to its relationship endpoint. Add or remove individual members instead, if the relationship allows that.
FULL_REPLACEMENT_PROHIBITED.exampleDetail: Full replacement of relationship 'tags' is prohibited!

INCLUSION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED.title: Inclusion depth exceeded
INCLUSION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED.description: An `include` path nests more relationships than the server allows. Shorten the path and fetch the deeper resources with a separate request.
INCLUSION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED.exampleDetail: Included paths 'author.publisher.country' exceed the maximum include depth of 2 permitted by the endpoint!

INCLUSION_NOT_ALLOWED.title: Inclusion is not allowed
INCLUSION_NOT_ALLOWED.description: An `include` path names a relationship that exists but may not be included from this request. Remove the path and fetch the related resources with a separate request.
INCLUSION_NOT_ALLOWED.exampleDetail: Included paths 'author.company' are not allowed by the endpoint!

INCLUSION_UNRECOGNIZED.title: Inclusion is unrecognized
INCLUSION_UNRECOGNIZED.description: An `include` path names a relationship the resource type does not have. Check each path against the relationships the type documents.
INCLUSION_UNRECOGNIZED.exampleDetail: Included paths 'auther' can't be recognized by the endpoint!

INCLUSION_UNSUPPORTED.title: Inclusion is unsupported
INCLUSION_UNSUPPORTED.description: This endpoint does not support the `include` parameter. Remove it and fetch related resources with separate requests.
INCLUSION_UNSUPPORTED.exampleDetail: Inclusion is not supported by the endpoint!

LOCAL_ID_CONFLICT.title: Local id conflict
LOCAL_ID_CONFLICT.description: Two operations in the Atomic Operations request create resources of the same type under the same `lid`. Give each resource a batch creates its own `lid`.
LOCAL_ID_CONFLICT.exampleDetail: Local id 'new-article' is already registered for type 'articles'!

LOCAL_ID_NOT_FOUND.title: Local id not found
LOCAL_ID_NOT_FOUND.description: An operation refers to a `lid` that no earlier operation in the batch created. Create the resource under that `lid` in an earlier operation, or refer to an existing resource by `id`.
LOCAL_ID_NOT_FOUND.exampleDetail: No resource is registered for local id 'new-article' of type 'articles'!

LOCAL_ID_NOT_SUPPORTED.title: Local id is not supported
LOCAL_ID_NOT_SUPPORTED.description: The request used a `lid`, which only means something inside an Atomic Operations request. Identify the resource by `id`, or send the dependent writes together as one atomic batch if the API offers the extension.
LOCAL_ID_NOT_SUPPORTED.exampleDetail: A local id (lid) is only supported within an Atomic Operations request; a standalone request must identify a resource by id.

MEDIA_TYPE_UNACCEPTABLE.title: The provided media type is unacceptable
MEDIA_TYPE_UNACCEPTABLE.description: Every `application/vnd.api+json` entry in the `Accept` header carries a parameter other than `ext` or `profile`, or asks for an `ext` the server does not support. Accept `application/vnd.api+json` with no other parameters.
MEDIA_TYPE_UNACCEPTABLE.exampleDetail: The media type 'application/vnd.api+json; version=2' is unacceptable in the 'Accept' header!

MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED.title: The provided media type is unsupported
MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED.description: The `Content-Type` is missing or names a media type the endpoint does not accept, or is `application/vnd.api+json` with a media type parameter other than `ext` or `profile`, or with an `ext` the server does not support. Send a JSON:API document as `Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json` with only the parameters the server supports.
MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED.exampleDetail: The media type 'application/vnd.api+json; charset=utf-8' is unsupported in the 'Content-Type' header!

NO_RESOURCE_REGISTERED.title: No resource registered
NO_RESOURCE_REGISTERED.description: The server tried to use a resource type it has nothing registered for, which is a configuration fault on its side. Retrying won't help; report it to the API's maintainers.
NO_RESOURCE_REGISTERED.exampleDetail: No resource is registered for type "articles".

PAGINATION_KIND_UNKNOWN.title: Pagination kind is not supported
PAGINATION_KIND_UNKNOWN.description: `page[kind]` names a pagination strategy this collection does not offer. Use one of the strategies the `detail` lists, or leave `page[kind]` out.
PAGINATION_KIND_UNKNOWN.exampleDetail: The pagination strategy 'page[kind]=offset' is not supported; use one of: page, cursor.

QUERY_PARAM_MALFORMED.title: Query parameter is malformed
QUERY_PARAM_MALFORMED.description: A query parameter has the wrong shape, such as `fields` sent without a type key or `include` sent as a list instead of a comma-separated string. Fix the parameter named in `source.parameter`.

QUERY_PARAM_UNRECOGNIZED.title: Query parameter is unrecognized
QUERY_PARAM_UNRECOGNIZED.description: The request used a query parameter this endpoint does not recognize. Remove it, or check its spelling against the parameters the API documents.
QUERY_PARAM_UNRECOGNIZED.exampleDetail: Query parameter 'colour' can't be recognized by the endpoint!

RELATED_ATTRIBUTE_OWNER_MISSING.title: Related attribute owner missing
RELATED_ATTRIBUTE_OWNER_MISSING.description: The request wrote an attribute the server stores on a related resource, and that related resource does not exist. Set the relationship first, or leave the attribute out.
RELATED_ATTRIBUTE_OWNER_MISSING.exampleDetail: Cannot write attribute "city": its related "address" is not present.

RELATIONSHIP_COUNT_NOT_ALLOWED.title: Relationship count is not allowed
RELATIONSHIP_COUNT_NOT_ALLOWED.description: `withCount` names a relationship that is not a countable to-many relationship of this resource. Ask for counts only on the relationships the API marks as countable.
RELATIONSHIP_COUNT_NOT_ALLOWED.exampleDetail: Counted relationships 'author' are not countable to-many relationships of this resource!

RELATIONSHIP_NOT_EXISTS.title: The requested relationship does not exist!
RELATIONSHIP_NOT_EXISTS.description: The request names a relationship this resource type does not have, or one whose endpoint the API does not expose. Check the relationship name against the ones the type documents.
RELATIONSHIP_NOT_EXISTS.exampleDetail: The requested relationship 'reviewers' does not exist!

RELATIONSHIP_TYPE_INAPPROPRIATE.title: Relationship type is inappropriate
RELATIONSHIP_TYPE_INAPPROPRIATE.description: The relationship data has the wrong cardinality: a list for a to-one relationship, a single identifier for a to-many one, or a `POST` or `DELETE` to a to-one relationship endpoint. Send linkage that matches the relationship.
RELATIONSHIP_TYPE_INAPPROPRIATE.exampleDetail: The provided relationship 'author' is of type of to-many, but to-one is expected!

REMOVAL_PROHIBITED.title: Removal is prohibited
REMOVAL_PROHIBITED.description: This relationship does not let a client remove members from it or clear it. Don't retry the request; the relationship changes only in the ways the API documents for it.

REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON.title: Request body is an invalid JSON document
REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON.description: The request body is not well-formed JSON. Fix the syntax the `detail` reports and send the request again.
REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON.exampleDetail: Request body is an invalid JSON document: 'Syntax error'!

REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON_API.title: Request body is an invalid JSON:API document
REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON_API.description: The request body is JSON but breaks the JSON:API document structure or the schema the server validates this resource against. Each violation is its own error, with `source.pointer` set where the server could locate it.
REQUEST_BODY_INVALID_JSON_API.exampleDetail: The data must match the type: object

REQUIRED_TOP_LEVEL_MEMBERS_MISSING.title: Required top-level members are missing
REQUIRED_TOP_LEVEL_MEMBERS_MISSING.description: The request body is not a JSON object, or has none of the top-level members `data`, `errors` and `meta`. Send a JSON object with the resource under `data`.
REQUIRED_TOP_LEVEL_MEMBERS_MISSING.exampleDetail: A document must contain at least one of the following top-level members: "data", "errors", "meta"

RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_ID_INVALID.title: Resource identifier ID is invalid
RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_ID_INVALID.description: A resource identifier in the request carries an `id` that is not a string, such as a number. Send every `id` as a JSON string.
RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_ID_INVALID.exampleDetail: The resource ID must be a string instead of integer!

RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_ID_MISSING.title: An ID for the resource identifier is missing
RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_ID_MISSING.description: A resource identifier in the request has neither an `id` nor a `lid`. Identify each related resource by its `id`, or by a `lid` inside an Atomic Operations request.
RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_ID_MISSING.exampleDetail: An ID or local ID (lid) for the resource identifier must be included!

RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_LID_INVALID.title: Resource identifier local ID is invalid
RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_LID_INVALID.description: A resource identifier in the request carries a `lid` that is not a string. Send every `lid` as a JSON string.
RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_LID_INVALID.exampleDetail: The resource local ID (lid) must be a string instead of integer!

RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_TYPE_INVALID.title: Resource identifier type is invalid
RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_TYPE_INVALID.description: A resource identifier in the request carries a `type` that is not a string. Send every `type` as a JSON string.
RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_TYPE_INVALID.exampleDetail: The resource type must be a string instead of integer!

RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_TYPE_MISSING.title: A type for the resource identifier is missing
RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_TYPE_MISSING.description: A resource identifier in the request has no `type`. Add the related resource's `type` to every identifier.
RESOURCE_IDENTIFIER_TYPE_MISSING.exampleDetail: A type for the resource identifier must be included!

RESOURCE_ID_CONFLICT.title: Resource id conflict
RESOURCE_ID_CONFLICT.description: The `id` in the update body is not the `id` in the URL. Send the id of the resource the URL addresses as `data.id`.
RESOURCE_ID_CONFLICT.exampleDetail: Resource id '12' does not match the endpoint id '7'!

RESOURCE_ID_INVALID.title: Resource ID is invalid
RESOURCE_ID_INVALID.description: The resource object's `id` is not a string, such as a number. Send `data.id` as a JSON string.
RESOURCE_ID_INVALID.exampleDetail: The resource ID must be a string instead of integer!

RESOURCE_ID_MISSING.title: Resource ID is missing
RESOURCE_ID_MISSING.description: The update request's resource object has no `id`. Include the id of the resource being updated as `data.id`.
RESOURCE_ID_MISSING.exampleDetail: A resource ID must be included in the document!

RESOURCE_ID_UNDECODABLE.title: Resource ID is undecodable
RESOURCE_ID_UNDECODABLE.description: The client-generated `id` is not in a format the server can decode into one of its own ids. Send an `id` in the format the API documents for this resource type.
RESOURCE_ID_UNDECODABLE.exampleDetail: The resource ID 'not-an-id' could not be decoded!

RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.title: Resource not found
RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.description: The resource the request addresses does not exist. Check the type and id in the URL; a deleted resource stays not found.
RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.exampleDetail: The requested resource is not found!

RESOURCE_TYPE_MISSING.title: Resource type is missing
RESOURCE_TYPE_MISSING.description: The resource object in `data` has no `type`. Add the type of the resource the endpoint serves.
RESOURCE_TYPE_MISSING.exampleDetail: A resource type must be included in the document!

RESOURCE_TYPE_UNACCEPTABLE.title: Resource type is unacceptable
RESOURCE_TYPE_UNACCEPTABLE.description: The `type` in the request is not one this endpoint or relationship accepts. Send the type the endpoint serves, or one the relationship documents for its related resources.

RESPONSE_BODY_INVALID_JSON.title: Response body is an invalid JSON document
RESPONSE_BODY_INVALID_JSON.description: The server produced a response body that is not valid JSON, which is a fault on its side. Retrying won't help; report it to the API's maintainers.
RESPONSE_BODY_INVALID_JSON.exampleDetail: Response body is an invalid JSON document: 'Syntax error'!

RESPONSE_BODY_INVALID_JSON_API.title: Response body is an invalid JSON:API document
RESPONSE_BODY_INVALID_JSON_API.description: The server produced a response that breaks the JSON:API document structure, which is a fault on its side. Retrying won't help; report it to the API's maintainers.
RESPONSE_BODY_INVALID_JSON_API.exampleDetail: The data must match the type: object

SORTING_UNRECOGNIZED.title: Sorting parameter is unrecognized
SORTING_UNRECOGNIZED.description: The `sort` parameter names a field this endpoint cannot sort by. Sort only on the fields the API documents for this resource type.
SORTING_UNRECOGNIZED.exampleDetail: Sorting parameter 'popularity' can't be recognized by the endpoint!

SORTING_UNSUPPORTED.title: Sorting is unsupported
SORTING_UNSUPPORTED.description: This endpoint does not support sorting. Remove the `sort` parameter.
SORTING_UNSUPPORTED.exampleDetail: Sorting is not supported by the endpoint!

TOP_LEVEL_MEMBERS_INCOMPATIBLE.title: Top-level members are incompatible
TOP_LEVEL_MEMBERS_INCOMPATIBLE.description: The request body has both `data` and `errors` at the top level, which JSON:API forbids. Send the resource under `data` alone.
TOP_LEVEL_MEMBERS_INCOMPATIBLE.exampleDetail: The members "data" and "errors" cannot coexist in the same document

TOP_LEVEL_MEMBER_NOT_ALLOWED.title: Top-level member is not allowed
TOP_LEVEL_MEMBER_NOT_ALLOWED.description: The request body has a top-level `included` member but no `data`. Remove `included`, or send it alongside `data`.
TOP_LEVEL_MEMBER_NOT_ALLOWED.exampleDetail: If a document does not contain a top-level "data" key, the "included" member must not be present either.
